text.title: llamaindex-production-gotchas Core Rules
text.summary: Rules patching known LlamaIndex production failure modes: async blocking, retriever concurrency, ReAct error handling, eval cost, observability.

rule.statement: Inside async endpoints, always call .aquery() not .query(). The sync .query() blocks the event loop and causes head-of-line blocking.
rule.rationale: FastAPI workers hanging in production traced to .query() inside async def; .aquery() resolves it.

rule.statement: Wrap SubQuestionQueryEngine.query() in asyncio.to_thread when calling from an async context; or call .aquery_engine. Sub-question fan-out is unbounded by default.
rule.rationale: SubQuestion engine internally fans out; bound concurrency or move to a thread pool.

rule.statement: QueryFusionRetriever must be capped at num_workers=4-8. Default is unbounded and trips rate-limit cliffs.
rule.rationale: Unbounded fusion opens 30+ concurrent LLM calls on the first multi-query request.

rule.statement: Wrap every ReActAgent tool with try/except that returns a structured error string. ReActAgent does not auto-recover from tool exceptions.
rule.rationale: A failing tool currently propagates as an unhandled exception, killing the agent loop.

rule.statement: Sample eval sets proportionally to budget (10-50 per metric per build); never run full faithfulness+relevancy+correctness on the entire set every CI run.
rule.rationale: A single full eval run on 1k samples can cost over $80 on GPT-4-class judges.

rule.statement: Wire LlamaIndex Callbacks (TokenCountingHandler + custom observability) at app boot. Untraced LlamaIndex runs are blind.
rule.rationale: Without callbacks you cannot answer 'why did this query cost $0.30?' after the fact.

rule.statement: Use response.print_response_stream() only when streaming is configured at the query_engine level. Mixing modes corrupts output.
rule.rationale: Streaming must be opted-in at engine construction; partial streaming corrupts the response buffer.

rule.statement: Cache embeddings at the IngestionPipeline boundary (cache=IngestionCache(...)); never embed inline in a query path.
rule.rationale: Inline embedding on every query adds 200-500ms; cache it once at ingestion.

rule.statement: When async is true (FastAPI / asyncio serving path) AND components_used includes the full gotcha set (SubQuestionQueryEngine, QueryFusionRetriever, ReActAgent and an eval loop), the hardening-record MUST contain every patch, each with its detector result: .aquery() on every engine call with no sync .query() in an async def (r1, fm-01 load test of 50 concurrent requests); SubQuestionQueryEngine driven through its async path with use_async=True and the fan-out bounded by an asyncio.Semaphore of 8 (r2); QueryFusionRetriever num_workers between 4 and 8 with a concurrency alert at 12 (r3, fm-02); every ReAct tool wrapped to return a structured error string and max_iterations pinned (r4, fm-03 fault injection); eval sampled at 10-50 items per metric per build (r5, fm-04); and TokenCountingHandler wired at boot with a per-turn check that aborts the turn when the running cost reaches cost_cap_per_turn_usd (r6). A record missing any one of these six is invalid on this branch.

rationale.source: LlamaIndex documentation (async query engines, QueryFusionRetriever, ReActAgent, TokenCountingHandler); Python asyncio documentation

rule.rationale: The four gotchas compound: a sub-question fan-out that runs a fusion retriever per sub-question multiplies concurrent LLM calls, and one failing tool inside that tree kills the whole agent loop. With all of them in one process the per-turn cost cap is the only backstop that turns a runaway into a bounded loss, which is why the callback check is mandatory rather than advisory.

rule.statement: When async is true BUT components_used is a subset of the gotcha set, the hardening-record MUST apply the universal patches and then one named patch per component actually present, with an explicit 'not-in-stack' entry for each absent one: .aquery() everywhere in async code (r1); TokenCountingHandler plus observability callbacks at boot with the per-turn cost compared to cost_cap_per_turn_usd (r6); embeddings cached at the IngestionPipeline boundary (r8); then SubQuestionQueryEngine -> r2, QueryFusionRetriever -> r3, ReActAgent -> r4, eval loop -> r5, whichever the profile lists. The 50-concurrent-request fm-01 test is mandatory regardless of components; component-specific detectors run only for listed components.

rationale.source: LlamaIndex documentation (async usage, callbacks and observability)

rule.rationale: Head-of-line blocking (fm-01) needs no exotic component, only one sync .query() inside an async def, so that patch and the cost telemetry are unconditional. Forcing 'not-in-stack' entries stops the record from silently omitting a component that was added after the hardening pass and never patched.

rule.statement: When async is low (LlamaIndex work runs in synchronous worker processes such as Celery or a batch CLI, and any async edge only dispatches jobs), the hardening-record MUST state that sync .query() is confined to worker processes and that every async endpoint reaching an engine delegates through asyncio.to_thread or run_in_executor (r1, r2); MUST record the concurrency bound as worker_count x num_workers and cap QueryFusionRetriever num_workers at 4 if fusion is present (r3); MUST still wrap ReAct tools if ReAct is present (r4), sample eval at 10-50 per metric (r5) and wire TokenCountingHandler (r6). Streaming (r7) MUST NOT be enabled in worker processes since there is no client to stream to.

rationale.source: LlamaIndex documentation (query engines, TokenCountingHandler); Python asyncio documentation (running blocking code in threads)

rule.rationale: In a sync worker the event-loop gotcha is moot, but the rate-limit cliff moves: N workers each running a fusion retriever with num_workers=8 open 8N concurrent LLM calls, which is the fm-02 failure with a different multiplier. The cost and error-handling patches are cheaper than the incidents they prevent regardless of the execution model.
